cards.power: The Level-Setter. Refuses to stand, dissolving the Authority Wall.
cards.lore: Decreases perceived power imbalance. Sitting signals you have nowhere else to be, even if you only have 2 minutes.
cards.gradeReason: Sit down, be at eye level. Physical move, zero interpretation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor llama sitting on tiny stool at patient bedside. Style: whimsical medical. Subject: eye-level consultation. Mood: warm, disarming.

cards.power: The Validation-Loop. Repeats the last 3 words of the wrestler's sentence.
cards.lore: Proves signal received; encourages the patient's Initial-Sprint without interruption.
cards.gradeReason: Repeat last 3 words. Concrete move, instant to deploy at any table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Brilliant parrot with stethoscope echoing speech bubbles back. Style: vivid tropical watercolor. Subject: active listening loop. Mood: attentive, electric.

cards.power: The Story-Scoop. Never asks Yes/No. Shuts his mouth for 60 seconds.
cards.lore: Avoids the Framing-Trap; catches the Actual-Problem instead of the expected one.
cards.gradeReason: Ask open question, shut up 60 seconds. Fully embodiable immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Walrus casting huge fishing net in clinic waiting room. Style: comic watercolor. Subject: open questioning stance. Mood: patient, expansive.

cards.power: The Storm-Soother. Doesn't fix the problem; names the feeling.
cards.lore: Affect labeling effect. Naming a Vague-Emotion moves activity from the Fear-Center to the Logic-Center.
cards.gradeReason: Clear move but naming the right emotion requires situational read of the patient.
cards.artworkPrompt: Nightingale in storm cloud, labeling lightning bolts with emotion words. Style: delicate ink wash. Subject: affect labeling. Mood: gentle, clarifying.

cards.power: The Jargon-Crusher. Uses Human-Words.
cards.lore: Cognitive load reduction. If Lore is too complex, the Wrestler ignores the Pill-Manual outside the arena.
cards.gradeReason: Be the sloth: slow down, plain words. The character IS the instruction.
cards.artworkPrompt: Sloth erasing medical jargon off a blackboard with pharmacy pills. Style: soft watercolor. Subject: plain language teaching. Mood: gentle, patient.

cards.power: The Option-Offer. Offers two viable moves.
cards.lore: Autonomy-Bait. Wrestlers are far more likely to wear the armor they choose to walk into battle.
cards.gradeReason: Solid concept but offering meaningful options requires clinical scaffolding first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Chimp holding two shields for patient to choose. Style: dynamic watercolor. Subject: shared decision making. Mood: collaborative, empowering.

cards.power: The Doubt-Digger. Digs for the hidden No.
cards.lore: Normalizes non-adherence. Removes the Guilt-Default to find the Real-Reason.
cards.gradeReason: Ask which meds are NOT being taken — brave, direct, instantly performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Squirrel digging up hidden pill bottles in forest floor. Style: earthy watercolor. Subject: non-adherence discovery. Mood: non-judgmental, curious.

cards.power: The Spark-Howl. Asks readiness scale (1 to 10) instead of barking orders.
cards.lore: Evokes internal motivation. Wrestlers must find their own Why.
cards.gradeReason: The readiness-scale move is specific but motivational interviewing needs session framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Wolf howling at patient holding readiness-scale thermometer. Style: dramatic watercolor. Subject: motivational interviewing. Mood: urgent, searching.

cards.power: The Quill-Retract. Delivers Heavy-Truth in slow, checked pieces.
cards.lore: Information Titration. Dumping Malignant-Max news all at once shuts down the Brain-Basket.
cards.gradeReason: Deliver bad news in slow checked pieces. The quill metaphor IS the technique.
cards.artworkPrompt: Porcupine carefully extending one quill at a time to anxious patient. Style: tender watercolor. Subject: breaking bad news titration. Mood: careful, compassionate.

cards.power: The Calm-Gravity. Absorbs Rage-Rhythm without Damage.
cards.lore: Parasympathetic mirroring. If the Strategist-Stays in Recovery-Mode, the Aggressor self-deregulates to match.
cards.gradeReason: Be the panda: absorb rage, stay calm. Zero-move character embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Meditating panda in hospital hallway absorbing lightning bolts from angry patient. Style: serene ink wash. Subject: de-escalation presence. Mood: unshakeable, warm.

cards.power: The Wisdom-Pause. Proves Time-the-Healer is better than a Radiation-Blast.
cards.lore: Manages tolerance of Uncertainty. Shifts goal from Immediate-Answer to Safe-Observation.
cards.gradeReason: Clear role but tolerating uncertainty requires clinical judgment to know when it applies.
cards.artworkPrompt: Owl on perch holding pocket watch, patient and rabbit waiting patiently below. Style: wise watercolor. Subject: watchful waiting. Mood: calm, measured.

cards.power: The Graceful-Exit. When the Terminal-Clock runs low, Shifts Peace Instinct of Winning.
cards.lore: Goal Alignment. Shifts from Disease-Centered to Dignity-Centered care.
cards.gradeReason: Shift from curing to dignity. The sunset metaphor hits immediately — universally felt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Swan gliding on river at sunset through hospital window with wilting flowers. Style: luminous watercolor. Subject: palliative care transition. Mood: bittersweet, graceful.

cards.power: The Language-Labyrinth. Leaves wrestlers in a Daze-Confusion, unable to follow the Playbook.
cards.lore: The Curse of Knowledge. Jaguar assumes fluent High-Linguistic code, unable to follow the Playbook.
cards.gradeReason: Strong villain character but recognizing your own jargon requires a self-awareness layer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Jaguar stalking through dense jungle of medical abbreviations and Latin terms. Style: dark watercolor. Subject: jargon-as-weapon. Mood: bewildering, predatory.

cards.power: The Time-Theft. Stands ready to exit, applying Urgency-Pressure.
cards.lore: Non-verbal Shut-Down signal. Tells the wrestler their Story-Illness are not worth the Doctor's time.
cards.gradeReason: That hand-on-door moment — every clinician knows it instantly. Zero explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Dingo in white coat reaching for door handle while patient opens mouth behind them. Style: sharp ink. Subject: premature exit move. Mood: awkward, charged.

cards.power: The Dictator-Bear. Gives Orders, not Choices. Treats wrestler like a Servant-Hamster.
cards.lore: Dominance-based care ignores personal values, breeding Internal-Resentment.
cards.gradeReason: Vivid villain archetype but playing the anti-move requires deliberate inversion.
cards.artworkPrompt: Lion in white coat pointing commanding finger at tiny hamster-patient. Style: bold watercolor. Subject: medical paternalism. Mood: oppressive, satirical.

cards.power: The Pattern-Lock. Labels patient Drug-Seeking, shutting down the Differential-Engine.
cards.lore: Counter-transference. the own Frustration-Sparks hide the Real-Antagonist behind Behavioral-Mask.
cards.gradeReason: DIFFICULT stamp is iconic visual but recognizing own bias needs a reflective framing layer.
cards.artworkPrompt: Leopard stamping DIFFICULT on patient file, spots forming question marks. Style: sharp watercolor. Subject: implicit bias labeling. Mood: uncomfortable, revealing.

cards.power: The Narrative-Block. Answers every question, hiding the Wrestler's-True-Signal.
cards.lore: Proxy-Interference; requires Sideloading the Gorilla to hear the true patient narrative.
cards.gradeReason: Clear role archetype but the sideloading strategy needs facilitation to execute.
cards.artworkPrompt: Gorilla blocking small badger-patient behind them, speaking to doctor alone. Style: ink watercolor. Subject: overbearing relative obstruction. Mood: protective-but-blocking.

cards.power: The Cultural-Cabling. Translates meaning and Lore, not just the Story-Swap.
cards.lore: 10x safer than Family-Member-Funnels; beats the Lost-in-Translation-Glitch.
cards.gradeReason: Build-bridges role is clear but only applies in specific language-barrier situations.
cards.artworkPrompt: Beaver building wooden bridge between doctor and patient from different cultural backgrounds. Style: warm watercolor. Subject: medical interpretation role. Mood: bridging, purposeful.

cards.power: The I-Don't-Know Move. Admits missing Name-Tags for the enemy.
cards.lore: Vulnerability-Credibility. Trust-Armor protects the partnership when tests come back negative.
cards.gradeReason: Say 'I don't know.' Three words, maximum bravery. Instant and complete.
cards.artworkPrompt: Tiny hummingbird hovering, speaking I DON'T KNOW to large bear-patient. Style: delicate ink wash. Subject: admitting diagnostic uncertainty. Mood: vulnerable, honest.

cards.power: The Echo-Check. Asks patient to explain the Pill-Move back to them.
cards.lore: Closes the loop; shifts responsibility from the Wrestler's-Memory to the Strategist's-Explanation.
cards.gradeReason: Ask them to repeat it back. Direct action, immediately executable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Toucan with colorful beak pointing to patient explaining pill sequence back to doctor. Style: vivid watercolor. Subject: teach-back method. Mood: playful, confirming.

cards.power: The Sovereign-Flight. Wrestler has Final-Say over their Body + Soul.
cards.lore: Core of medical ethics. the Wrestler owns the Ring, even if the Doctor disagrees.
cards.gradeReason: Powerful principle but enacting patient autonomy in practice needs situational framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Eagle carrying patient wishes scroll, soaring above hospital. Style: KayfaBIZARRO bold watercolor. Subject: patient rights and autonomy. Mood: sovereign, majestic.

cards.power: The Protective-Hug. Always acts to increase Health-Tokens.
cards.lore: Duty to act in Patient's interest, the primal Healer-Impulse.
cards.gradeReason: Warm principle but acting in patient's best interest requires clinical definition each time.
cards.artworkPrompt: Enormous bear hugging small patient protectively in hospital room. Style: KayfaBIZARRO bold watercolor. Subject: beneficence principle. Mood: fiercely caring.

cards.power: The Fair-Scan. Defeats Hierarchy-Walls so the Poor-Wrestler gets the MRI-High-Tech.
cards.lore: Ensures Arena-Resources are shared fairly across the entire Social Map.
cards.gradeReason: Most abstract ethics principle — distributive justice has no single performable micro-move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Giraffe towering over hospital, distributing MRI tokens equally to all animals below. Style: KayfaBIZARRO bold watercolor. Subject: distributive justice. Mood: equalizing, systemic.

cards.power: The Venom-Block. Slaps Aggressive-Surgical Options if Risk > Gain.
cards.lore: Primum non nocere, the primary Safety-Brake of the Hippocratic.
cards.gradeReason: Do-no-harm instinct is clear but Risk > Gain calculus is always case-by-case.
cards.artworkPrompt: Mongoose in defensive stance blocking surgical instruments with shield. Style: KayfaBIZARRO bold watercolor. Subject: non-maleficence principle. Mood: vigilant, protective.

cards.power: The Soul-Connector.
cards.lore: Put down the clipboard, look them in the eye. They aren't a Case, they are a Wrestler. Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Meta-orchestrator card — integrating the whole deck is the move, but it requires mastery.
cards.artworkPrompt: FrizzleBob in white coat conducting orchestra of animal clinicians in hospital hallway. Style: whimsical watercolor. Subject: integrative clinical presence. Mood: joyful, commanding.

verdict: Bedside Ballet is the most immediately playable MedKayfab deck — eleven G1 cards in a clinical communication set is almost unheard of. The animal-naming system does real pedagogical work: Low-Stool-Llama and Zen-Panda-Prime ARE their technique. The KayfaBIZARRO ethics crossover on page 7 is a structural genius move. Justice-the-Giraffe is the one card that cannot find its micro-move. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: 25 animal archetypes that teach every clinical communication skill from open questions to breaking bad news — for med students, residents, and anyone who has ever grabbed a door handle too soon.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: THE BEDSIDE BALLET – Clinical Communication as a Contact Sport (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

25 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master the open question, the bad-news conversation, and the four bioethics principles that decide who actually gets the final say.

Medicine grades you on the molecule, the dose, and the lab value. It almost never grades you on the sentence you wrap around them, even though the sentence is the only part the patient takes home. So communication gets quietly filed under personality, something you either have or you do not, and nobody drills the one thing that every complaint, every refused treatment, and every "but the other doctor said" actually turns on. The result is the door-handle moment: hand on the door, exit in sight, and only then does the patient say the thing they walked in to say.

The Bedside Ballet treats the consultation as choreography you can rehearse, a story-wrestling match where every skill and every bad habit walks in as a character with a tell. Stop hoping you are a "natural." Start drilling the move.

YOU'LL GET
- 25 illustrated MedKayfab cards (4 cards per page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like Zen-Panda-Prime, Honest-Hummingbird, and Door-Handle-Dingo
- Hero cards and villain anti-patterns in the same deck, so the table argues about which one it just watched
- A KayfaBizarro ethics crossover for the four bioethics principles
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
This deck personifies the part of medicine that happens above the collarbones. You will meet Zen-Panda-Prime, who holds the silence after a hard question instead of rushing to fill it, and Honest-Hummingbird, who delivers bad news in small true sentences rather than one long evasive paragraph. Then there is Door-Handle-Dingo, the anti-pattern who only hears the real complaint as the consultation is already ending. Heroes and villains share the deck on purpose, because most of clinical communication is recognizing which one you are being in the moment.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor: the Character (the skill or the trap), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (when to use it, what it costs), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the conversation you have to win). Mechanism Flash is the brutal part here: say the actual sentence out loud, in one breath, the way you would say it to a frightened human, or the consultation on the Stage falls apart. The synthesis page raises the stakes with three combo Quests, the Jargon-Daze, the Rage-Riot, and the Final-Bell, where you stack skills against the hardest rooms on the ward.

Honest cognitive load
This is a foundational deck, lighter on biochemistry and heavier on nerve. It suits early medical students building bedside manner, residents prepping for OSCE communication stations, and anyone who has ever grabbed the door handle too soon. It pairs naturally with Psychiatry for the conversations that fight back, and with any clinical deck you already own, since communication is the wrapper around every diagnosis you will ever deliver.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free. If you find it useful, a fair price is €5. If you are a student on a budget, enter €0, no questions asked. If you want to support more decks, anything above fair price is appreciated. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
MedKayfab is a learning companion, not a clinical reference. Content was created by a physician and reviewed to the best of our knowledge, but medicine evolves, guidelines change, and some mechanisms in here will be simplified or wrong. Always verify against current primary sources and clinical guidelines before applying anything to patient care. The Blödsinn! is the vehicle. The science is serious.

Stay fluffy. — Doc FrizzleBob
